translations.1: Then Jethro, the imām of Midian, the father-in-law of Moses, heard all that God had done for Moses and for Israel his people, since God had brought the sons of Israel out of Egypt.
translations.2: And Jethro, the father-in-law of Moses, took Zipporah, the wife of Moses, after he had sent her back to him.
translations.3: And her two sons — the name of one of whom was Gershom, because he said: 'I have become a stranger in a land of strangeness' —
translations.4: and the name of the other was Eliezer, because he said: 'The God of my father was in my help, and delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh.'
translations.5: And Jethro, the father-in-law of Moses, came with his sons and his wife to him, into the wilderness — he who was encamped there — at the mountain of God.
translations.6: And he sent someone to say to Moses on his behalf: 'Your father-in-law Jethro has come to you, and your wife and her two sons with her.'
translations.7: And Moses went out to receive his father-in-law; and he bowed down, then kissed him; and each man asked after the well-being of his companion; and the two of them entered into the tent.
translations.8: And Moses recounted to his father-in-law all that God had done to Pharaoh and the Egyptians on account of the sons of Israel, and all the hardship that had befallen them on the way — and how God had delivered them.
translations.9: And Jethro rejoiced over all the good that God had done for the sons of Israel, and that He had delivered them from the hand of the Egyptians.
translations.10: And Jethro said: 'Blessed be God, who has delivered you from the hand of the Egyptians and from the hand of Pharaoh — who has delivered the people from under the burden of the Egyptians.'
translations.11: 'Now I know that God is greater than all objects of worship, inasmuch as He requited them with the very thing by which they had acted presumptuously against them.'
translations.12: And Jethro, the father-in-law of Moses, presented burnt-offerings and sacrifices to God; and Aaron came, and all the elders of the sons of Israel, to eat a meal with him before God.
translations.13: And when it was on the morrow, Moses stood to judge the people; and the people stood before him from morning until evening.
translations.14: And his father-in-law saw all that he was doing for the people; and he said: 'What is this thing that you are doing for the people? What is your concern that you sit alone, while all the people stand before you from morning until evening?'
translations.15: He said to him: 'It is because the people come to me seeking the word of God.'
translations.16: 'If they have a dispute, they come to me, and I judge between the man and his companion, and I make known to them the ordinances of God and His laws.'
translations.17: His father-in-law said to him: 'What you are doing is not the best course.'
translations.18: 'You will surely wear out — both you and the people who are with you — for the matter is too heavy upon you, and you cannot do it alone.'
translations.19: 'Now, accept from me what I counsel you, and may God be with you: be you for the people the one who faces God — bring their matters up to Him;'
translations.20: 'and warn them concerning the ordinances and the laws, and make known to them the way in which they shall walk, and the deeds that they shall do.'
translations.21: 'And you — look out from all the people for men of ability, who fear God, men of integrity who hate greed; and appoint over them heads of thousands and hundreds, and of fifties and of tens.'
translations.22: 'And they shall judge among the people at all times; and every great matter they shall bring up to you, while every small matter they shall judge themselves — so lighten the burden from yourself, and they shall bear it together with you.'
translations.23: 'If you do this thing, and God commands you in it, you will be able to endure; and likewise all this people will reach their place in peace.'
translations.24: And Moses accepted from his father-in-law, and did all that he had commanded him.
translations.25: And Moses chose men of ability from all the house of Israel, and appointed them as heads over them — heads of thousands and hundreds, and of fifties and of tens.
translations.26: And they came to judge among the people at all times; every difficult matter they would bring up to Moses, and every small matter they would judge themselves.
translations.27: And Moses released his father-in-law, and he went on his way to his land.
